Definition: of Hebrew origin (H2696); Esrom (i.e. Chetsron), an Israelite:--Esrom.
BiblicalUsage: Esrṓm is the Greek form of Hezron, the son of Pharez in the line of Judah. He stands in the genealogy of Jesus in Matthew and Luke, between Pharez and Aram. His fuller story is on his People profile.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Esrom matters because the genealogy matters: God kept the line through ordinary men, and He named them.
